 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R

The present petitioners before this Court are the father-in- law and mother-in-law of the deceased,
who died of burn injuries in the intervening night of 13/14.05.1988 and a case was registered against the present petitioners as well as the husband of the deceased.
Apart from the present petitioners and the husband, there were three other accused, who were acquitted by the Trial Court.

Reason: The present petitioners (Bal Kishun and Paro Devi) were convicted by the Trial Court under Section 304B of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo 10 years rigorous imprisonment,

sentences.text: while their son (husband of the deceased) has been convicted under Sections 302/149 and 498A of the Indian Penal Code and had been sentenced to undergo Life Imprisonment.
In appeal, the High Court, while upholding the conviction of the present petitioners, has reduced the sentenced from 10 years to 07 years.
The High Court has converted the conviction of their son - Sunil Kumar from Section 302 IPC to Section 304B IPC and sentenced him to undergo 10 years rigorous imprisonment.
The Special Leave Petition filed by Sunil Kumar has already been dismissed by this Court vide order dated 19.07.2024 in SLP (Crl.) No. 9085/2024.
Vide order dated 26.07.2024, this Court issued notice in the present case only on the quantum of sentence.
The minimum sentence prescribed under Section 304B IPC is 07 years.
Moreover, the role of the petitioners in this case is also quite active.

Not only is there enough evidence against the petitioners, but more importantly, there is a Dying Declaration of the deceased, who has categorically stated the active role of the petitioners, when her husband poured kerosene oil on the deceased and burnt her.

Moreover, she has also stated in the Dying Declaration that even five months prior to the incident, another attempt was made, inter alia, by the present petitioners to burn her, which somehow could not succeed.
We have also gone through the evidence and the orders of the Trial Court as well as the High Court.
We have absolutely no doubt in our mind that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Under these circumstances, this case does not call for any interference.
The Special Leave Petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, is/are disposed of.

(JAYANT KUMAR ARORA) (RENU BALA GAMBHIR)
